_comment: Question set and routing logic for the Find services assessment. Pure data: the web page and the future voice agent both read this file, so neither may hold logic the other does not. Every scoring effect carries evidence.branch_condition, which is the verbatim condition string of a human-verified branch in data/organizations.json, and evidence.org_id, the organisation whose access_path that branch lives in. If an effect cannot point at a real branch, the effect does not exist. Weights: org effects 20-40, category effects 5-15. suppress uses a negative weight and demotes only; nothing is ever excluded from results.
privacy_notice: Nothing you enter here is saved or sent anywhere. The answers stay in this browser, they are not written to a file or a database, and closing the page loses them. We never ask for a name, a date of birth, an address or any policy or benefit number, and you can skip any question.
intro: A few questions to work out which of the organisations in this directory are likely to be useful, and in what order. Nothing is ever ruled out — answers move things up and down the list, they do not remove them. Where we have nothing to offer, we will say so instead of guessing. It takes about five minutes, and you can skip anything.

blocks.title: Eye care
blocks.preamble: Most of the rehabilitation services in here need a report from an eye doctor before they can start. These three questions are the ones that unblock the most people.

blocks.title: Everyday life
blocks.preamble: The next few questions are about things other than sight. We ask them because they usually decide whether any of the rest actually works — a rehabilitation plan is hard to start from an unsteady home, and none of it helps if there is no way to get there. Be warned: for several of these, this directory has nothing to offer, and it will say so plainly instead of inventing a referral. You can skip this whole section.

handoffs.headline: This directory has no housing services in it.
handoffs.body: That is a gap in what we have collected, not a claim that none exist. Every organisation in here is about sight loss, and none of them houses anyone. The county line below is free, answers immediately by phone, and is the right first call for housing, and it accepts a call from a family member or a professional on someone's behalf. It is not a vision service and does not pretend to be.
handoffs.missing_record_note: We do not have a verified NC 211 record yet, so we are not printing a number for it. NC 211 is the usual statewide route for housing, food and utility help, and it should be added to this directory and verified before we point anyone at it.

handoffs.headline: This directory has no food programmes in it.
handoffs.body: We collected sight-loss services, so food assistance is simply not here. Rather than guess, we are handing you to the county line, which is free and immediate by phone and can start a referral for someone else. Nothing in your sight-loss results changes because of this answer.
handoffs.missing_record_note: We do not have a verified NC 211 record, nor any verified food pantry or SNAP outreach record. Those would need to be added and checked against a published source before we name one.

handoffs.headline: This directory has no help with utility bills in it.
handoffs.body: Lighting matters a lot with low vision, so this is a real problem and not a side issue. We still have nothing verified to offer on it. The county line is free, answers by phone straight away, and is where utility assistance is usually started in Mecklenburg.
handoffs.missing_record_note: We do not have a verified NC 211 record, and no verified record for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Programme or the Crisis Intervention Programme. Do not quote a number for these until a record exists.

handoffs.headline: We have nobody in here who does benefits counselling.
handoffs.body: Working out whether someone qualifies for Medicaid, SSI or SSDI, and what happens to those benefits if they start work, is a specialist job. There is no record in this directory that does it. The one exception is VA benefits, which the veterans organisations in here do cover. For everything else the county line is the honest starting point.
handoffs.missing_record_note: No Social Security work-incentive or benefits-counselling record has been collected. A WIPA project or a certified benefits counsellor covering Mecklenburg would need to be researched and verified before we list one.

handoffs.headline: There is exactly one legal record in this directory, and this is it.
handoffs.body: When a disability service or an accommodation has been refused, this is the free legal route in North Carolina. We are showing it here as a hand-off rather than scoring it, because no organisation in this directory publishes a referral path into it — we found the record, but not a verified route. Intake can be reached by phone if the online form is not usable.
handoffs.missing_record_note: No organisation in this directory publishes a branch that routes a person to disability rights legal help, so this hand-off is based on the record itself rather than on a referral path someone else publishes. Worth asking the agencies whether they do refer, and to whom.

handoffs.headline: This directory does not cover general legal help.
handoffs.body: Housing court, family matters, debt, benefits appeals and criminal matters are all outside what we collected. We have one disability rights record and nothing else, and we would rather say that than send you somewhere we have not checked.
handoffs.missing_record_note: We do not have a verified Legal Aid of North Carolina record, nor a Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy record. Both are likely relevant and neither has been researched or verified yet.
